title: SCAFFOLD-DIST-001: close the silent default-branch fallback and pin a self-test
intent: The scaffolder was proven on one repository. Its four defects were all environment-coupling bugs invisible to reading, so environment variety across other repos is likely to expose more. Two gaps blocked wider distribution: a silent 'main' fallback that would write a confidently-wrong canonical instruction into any repo whose real default differs, and the absence of any test reproducing the conditions that produced the known defects.
behavior_change: A repository whose default branch cannot be detected no longer receives an AGENTS.md silently naming 'main'. It warns; headless it refuses with exit 3 unless --default-branch is supplied; interactively it asks. Repositories with a resolvable origin/HEAD or a local main/master behave exactly as before -- no new prompt, no new flag required. Separately, --force without --yes now resolves consent once BEFORE any write and refuses the whole run if it cannot, instead of skipping one file and writing another.

diff_articulation.what_changed: Flag 1: detect_default_branch returns (name, detected) instead of a bare string; main() adds --default-branch, warns on an undetected guess, refuses headlessly with exit 3, and prompts interactively. The 'preferred' shape was implemented rather than the 'minimum', because the preferred warning text names --default-branch and therefore requires the flag anyway -- warn-only would leave the poison pill in place, since nobody reads stderr mid-run in an agent session. Flag 3: scripts/ci/test_scaffold_agents_md.py, fourteen tests driving the real CLI as a subprocess against real temp git repos, plus a named step in core_ci.yml that pins it.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: The dev order specified tests/test_scaffold_agents_md.py. Grounding showed repo-root tests/ is collected by NO workflow -- every reference names an individual file or one subdirectory (tests/grounding_agent/), and the tests/ paths in core_ci and rmos_ci run after `cd services/api`, a different tree entirely. Placing the self-test there would have created it in precisely the uncollected location that produces the unpinned-test hazard. It lives in scripts/ci/ beside the already-pinned tests instead.

commands_run: A THIRD IMPLEMENTATION DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE NEW TEST, not by reading. --force without --yes returned 0 and wrote a file. Cause: on Windows, stdin redirected to NUL is a character device, so sys.stdin.isatty() returns TRUE and the headless guard never fired. Deferring the prompt into the write loop then produced a partial run -- the existing-file overwrite was correctly skipped while a different, non-conflicting file was written anyway, leaving the repo half-scaffolded under a --force that was never granted. Consent is now resolved ONCE before the loop and refusal aborts the whole run.
TEETH PROVEN (mandatory, Flag 1): reverting `return "main", False` to `return "main", True` turns test_undetectable_default_branch_refuses_headlessly RED at the assertion, then restored -> 14 passed.
TEETH PROVEN (regression, cheap): reverting detect_repo_name to repo.name turns test_heading_uses_remote_name_not_directory_name RED, then restored.
common case unchanged: dry-run against luthiers-toolbox still resolves main via origin/HEAD, still skips the existing PR template, no new prompt.

REQUIRED DoD STEP -- unlike-repo dry-run against Master-All-Strings (root pyproject.toml, src/ layout, its own remote): clean. It exercised the pyproject path luthiers-toolbox CANNOT, since this repo has no root pyproject, and correctly reported 'Detected requires-python = >=3.11'. No defect #5 surfaced. This step is required precisely because the fixtures encode only the four environments already known, and are by construction blind to the variety that is the actual distribution risk.
CI collection stated: scripts/ci/ is not collected wholesale; the new file is pinned by a named step in core_ci.yml alongside the CBSP21 ownership tests.

MANIFEST SCOPE: this branch carries two commits the owner ruled are ONE order -- the scaffolder and its distribution-hardening are the same deliverable. CBSP21 evaluates the PR diff rather than each commit, so two half-covering manifests scored 75%. This manifest therefore declares the whole branch diff; agents-md-scaffold.json is retained as the first increment's record rather than deleted.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Flag 2 (_run collapsing every failure to None, so 'git not installed', 'not a repo' and 'no remote configured' are indistinguishable) is recorded here as a named follow-up and deliberately not built. It is a diagnostics-granularity issue, not a wrong-output risk, and the dev order placed it out of scope.
